reason: The repository catalog says only that necessary and sufficient conditions for metrizability exist. Primary-source inspection now supplies two presentations: Nagata 1950 Theorem I states that a regular space is metrizable iff it satisfies beta-countability, defined using a countable open basis split into neighborhood-finite open coverings; Nagata 1957 Theorem 2 restates the Nagata-Smirnov result using an open basis that is a countable union of locally finite collections. Neither source defines historical 'regular' at the theorem locator in terms that are already crosswalked to mathlib's non-Hausdorff RegularSpace, and no accountable independent reviewer has approved a separation convention, the transport between beta-countability and the later sigma-locally-finite-basis formulation, or the role of per-layer coverings. RegularSpace plus T2Space and T3Space have different elaborated types whose equivalence needs a checked transport; choosing either source packaging or silently dropping the per-layer covering condition before the inherited intake review would risk changing the received proposition rather than elaborate an exact accepted target.
